messages:
maria: Hey team — running into a weird issue where our rerank pipeline starts returning vectors with inconsistent dims when we stream embeddings + paginate a large dataset. Happens only in Python client and only when batch size > 128. Anyone seen this?

josh: hmm — do you mean the numpy arrays have different shapes between items in the same batch, or the model returns variable-length embeddings?

maria: arrays. Example: most items are (1536,), but every ~50th item comes back (1024,) and downstream cosine sim fails. No obvious exceptions, just shape mismatch.

leo: couple quick checks: 1) are you accidentally concatenating partial streamed chunks before the final chunk? 2) tokenization mismatch if you're using two different embed models in the same run.

maria: good call. We're using client.embeddings.stream (python) to avoid memory spikes and a pagination helper that yields pages of docs. Here's the simplified flow:

```py
for page in pager():
    for batch in batcher(page, size=256):
        for resp in client.embeddings.stream(model=model, input=batch):
            store(resp.embedding)
```

josh: streaming embeddings is tricky — some clients emit partial "embedding" arrays while streaming tokens for large models. The stream typically emits incremental logits or tokens; the final embedding is only in the last message or non-streaming call. Which SDK version?

maria: using py-client 0.9.2. I assumed stream yields final vector objects for embeddings.

anya: that version had a bug where the streaming wrapper forwarded partial payloads for long inputs. Two options: upgrade to 0.9.4 (fixes streaming for embeddings), or switch to non-streaming embeddings.create which returns complete vectors per call.

maria: ok — we'll try upgrade. But even when reproducing locally with stream=False I still hit an occasional 1024-dim item when I interleave two different model ids in the same run (we do an A/B test). Could batching helper be merging responses across model requests?

leo: if you're reusing a mutable list for batch accumulation across model calls it's possible. Also watch out for numpy dtype and view/copy issues. Example bug: creating an output buffer with dtype=float32 and then assigning a shorter np.array into a slice can leave garbage if shapes differ.

maria: that makes sense. Another thing: our pager returns last page with size < batch_size. Could we be incorrectly padding or truncating?

josh: yes. If downstream code assumes fixed shape it might pad/truncate. Also check you don't have legacy rerank vector cache keyed by doc id of a different model — cache hits with wrong-dim vectors are common.

maria: new info — we saw a 401 mid-run from auth rotation around the same time, and our client retry logic reties the whole batch but with stream mode it sometimes yields mixed items (some from first attempt, some from retry). Any recommended pattern?

anya: for idempotency across retries: attach an idempotency_key per logical batch and make your client read the final-only responses (no incremental chunks). For streaming, if you get a 401 mid-stream you should discard partials and restart the entire request. The SDK v0.9.4 exposes a helper:

```py
with client.embeddings.create_stream(model=model, input=batch, idempotency_key=key) as s:
    final = s.get_final()  # blocks until full vector or raises
```

josh: also consider smaller batch sizes (64-128) for streaming to avoid mid-batch auth rotations, and set retry policy to exponential backoff with jitter. Example header-based retry marker we use: X-Request-Id + idempotency_key so server can dedupe.

maria: thanks. Quick question on language-specific quirk: our JS team saw consistent dims but Python team didn't. Anyone know a tokenizer pitfall?

leo: JS SDK was defaulting to model=embed-lite and Python to model=embed-large because env var was different. That explains dims difference. Make sure model param is explicitly passed and validated. Also add a check assert embedding.shape == expected_dim when storing — fail-fast.

maria: good plan. I'll: upgrade SDK, change stream->non-stream for embeddings during retries, add idempotency_key, assert dims, and reduce batch_size to 64.

anya: small helper PR idea: add a batcher utility that emits tuples (idempotency_key, batch) and a safe_store API that verifies dims before persisting. I can draft.

maria: pls do. I'll open a failing test and paste logs in the PR. TY! :thumbsup:

bot-ci: build started for branches/maria/emb-dim-fix — CI will run unit tests for batching-helper.

josh: also ping @eng-ml-ops to review any runtime tweaks if we need to change default retry window.

maria: will do. I'll update this thread with PR link and small repro script.
